stop_condition: Operator-scoped round: the diff since round 5 plus the new release-claims-check guard. Done when (1) the guard's sensitivity is proved by mutations its author did not write, its exemption escape hatches are probed, and its narrowing is tested against a real R5-F1-shaped defect; (2) R5-F1 and R5-F2's fixes are verified; (3) the manifest rows, rubric bump, completeness floor and tally are mechanically confirmed. NOT a fresh review of all four surfaces. Every finding classified against the operator's pre-registered split: false shipped claim = HIGH/blocking; added precision on a true claim = INFO/v5.0.1.

findings.location: docs/RELEASE_AUDIT.md:815 (DP9 bolded headline) and docs/RELEASE_AUDIT.md:864 (tally movement history)
findings.evidence: STOP-RULE SIDE: makes a shipped claim FALSE -> blocking. R5-F2 established that the coherence rollup's scope conjunct has TWO arms and only the live one dies over an empty change set. I re-derived this from source rather than from R5's text: scope_drift_json='$a - $d' (qa-gate.sh:16066) builds $a from actual_filtered_json, which comes from each unit's PERSISTED completion payload (:16019-16048), not the tracker, and pushes kind 'undeclared_scope'; under_coverage_json='$diff - $roll' (:16194) is fed by the live tracker (:16119) and pushes kind 'tracker_diff_mismatch'. The durable arm fires over an empty change set. The fix landed on FOUR surfaces and missed TWO. Corrected: CHANGELOG.md:46-56 ('an empty change set costs the UNDER-COVERAGE DIRECTION of scope, not scope as a whole'); README.md:228-233 ('Narrow. Scope is checked by two arms and only one reads the tracker'); the RELEASE_AUDIT bullet at :1032-1041; and DP9's own BODY ('the accurate statement is that an empty change set disables the UNDER-COVERAGE DIRECTION of scope, not the scope check as a whole ... An earlier draft of this cell said the conjunct "cannot fire" ... which OVERSTATED the defect'). NOT corrected: DP9's own BOLDED HEADLINE at :815 still reads 'THE ROLLUP HAS NEVER RUN ON A REAL TARGET, IN EITHER DIRECTION, AND ONE OF THE FOUR CONJUNCTS ABOVE CANNOT FIRE OVER AN EMPTY CHANGE SET'; and the tally movement history at :864 still reads 'one of its four conjuncts cannot fire over an empty change set'. A proposition sweep (grep -rniE 'conjunct' over every *.md) returns exactly these two as live assertions; the two other hits carrying this wording (RELEASE_AUDIT:1041, CHANGELOG:55) are explicitly labelled as retracted earlier drafts and are correct. VERIFICATION METHOD: this is an INFERENCE from reading control flow, not an observed run -- stated explicitly per the C9 criterion this same change set adds.
findings.description: The row's bolded headline asserts the exact wording its own body, four sentences below, identifies as the overstated earlier draft and retracts. The ledger is the document the release decision is read off, and a reader who stops at the bolded headline takes away that a whole conjunct of the coherence rollup is dead when in fact only one DIRECTION of one conjunct is. Under C9 (added in this change set) an overstated defect fails exactly as an understated one does. This is also the fifth consecutive round of the shape the LESSONS.md entry added in this same change set names -- 'a correction is scoped to a PROPOSITION, not to the location field of the finding that named it' -- and R5-F2 explicitly listed both :815 and :861 (now :864) among its six locations, so these are not surfaces nobody pointed at. The lesson's own worked example is 'in its own bolded headline, four sentences above its own body saying twice', which is this defect exactly. ALTERNATIVE READING, disclosed for symmetry: if 'the four conjuncts above' were read as the four ISSUE KINDS (incomplete, undeclared_scope, hash_divergence, tracker_diff_mismatch) rather than the four conjuncts of the row's own claim text, the sentence would be true, since tracker_diff_mismatch alone does die. I reject that reading because the document uses 'conjunct' consistently for the claim-text four (CHANGELOG:53 'the other three conjuncts (untested criterion, unmapped unit, moved artifact hash)'; DP9 body 'the scope conjunct is implemented by TWO arms'), and because the row's body names this precise phrasing as the retracted overstatement. Even under the charitable reading the sentence is ambiguous at the one point the release decision is read. FIX: at :815 and :864, replace 'one of the four conjuncts cannot fire over an empty change set' with 'an empty change set disables the UNDER-COVERAGE DIRECTION of the scope conjunct; the durable arm and the other three conjuncts still fire'.

findings.evidence: STOP-RULE SIDE: makes a shipped claim FALSE -> blocking. The header block documenting the inline exemption reads: 'An inline cross-reference to ANOTHER release's tally. Exempts only tokens on that line, so a line may carry a live figure and a reference to a different release and still be checked for the live one... which is why the marker exempts the LINE'. MEASURED, not inferred: I copied the shipped ledger, replaced the live figure at :905 with a stale one AND appended '<!-- tally-xref -->' to that line, and ran the shipped checker: rc=0, output 'OK: every surface agrees with the ledger rows.' The identical stale figure without the marker fires (rc=1, TOKEN:). The implementation is strip_exempt's 'if (line[i] ~ /<!-- *tally-xref *-->/) continue' at :157, which drops the WHOLE line. I confirmed the text reaches users: 'release-claims-check.sh --help' prints lines 1-60 via sed, and this block is lines 38-43, so it is in the help output.
findings.description: The middle clause asserts that a live figure sharing a line with an xref marker is still checked. It is not; the marker silences the entire line. The final clause of the same sentence ('which is why the marker exempts the LINE') states the true behaviour, so the passage asserts X and then not-X, and one of the two is false. The operational consequence is not cosmetic: an author who trusts the middle clause puts a live tally on an xref line and loses coverage silently -- which is exactly the R5-F1 defect class this tool was built to stop. The shipped ledger does NOT currently do this: the author split the sentence across :944 (live 8/9/0/1/18, checked) and :945 (xref 13/3/0/0/16, exempt), i.e. authoring practice already follows the line-granular reality rather than the header's middle clause. FIX: one sentence -- delete the 'so a line may carry a live figure ... still be checked for the live one' clause and state plainly that the marker exempts the whole line, so a live figure must be authored on a different line (as :944/:945 already does). DISCLOSED FOR SYMMETRY: if the operator reads the '...' as a rhetorical turn ('you might think X -- which is why actually Y'), the passage is merely unreadable rather than false, and this drops to INFO. I classify it HIGH because the natural reading is the false one and the failure it invites is silent.

findings.evidence: STOP-RULE SIDE: added precision on a true claim -> NOT blocking, v5.0.1 follow-up. MEASURED: I took the shipped ledger, rewrote the live sentence at :905 into R5-F1's ORIGINAL four-group form with R5-F1's original wrong figures (`9 / 8 / 0 / 1`), and ran the shipped checker: rc=0, 'OK: every surface agrees with the ledger rows.' So the guard as shipped would NOT have caught R5-F1 as R5-F1 actually occurred. It catches it only because the one live four-group sentence was rewritten to the five-group form in this same change set. I swept for remaining live four-group tokens in the current section: exactly two (:891, :898), both inside the TALLY-HISTORY block at 887-903, therefore legitimately exempt. So there is no live instance today.
findings.description: This is the operator's question (c) answered with evidence: yes, the narrowing to five-group tokens creates a blind spot that would let a real R5-F1-shaped defect through in its original form. It is NOT a false claim, and that is why it is INFO rather than HIGH: the script's own header states the narrowing and its reason accurately ('A TALLY TOKEN IS THE FIVE-GROUP FORM ONLY ... Where a live sentence used the four-group form it was normalised to carry its total, rather than widening the pattern'), and the measured justification for not widening (the broad pattern matched exit-code lists, doctor ranges and task-id runs) is sound. The residual risk is that the invariant 'every live tally is authored five-group' is now load-bearing and is enforced by nothing -- a future author writing `8 / 9 / 0 / 1` is invisible to the guard and will get a green 'OK: every surface agrees'. v5.0.1 options, cheapest first: (a) add a four-group DETECTOR that does not compare but emits a 'normalise this to five groups' advisory, so the invariant is self-enforcing; or (b) match four-group tokens only when the line also contains a ledger cue (`split`, `tally`, `NOT-PROVEN`), which sidesteps the exit-code/task-id false positives that motivated the narrowing.

findings.evidence: STOP-RULE SIDE: added precision on a true claim -> NOT blocking, v5.0.1 follow-up. MEASURED: strip_exempt sets hist=1 on a BEGIN and clears it only on an END, so an UNMATCHED BEGIN exempts everything from that line to the next END or EOF. I inserted a single '<!-- TALLY-HISTORY BEGIN -->' immediately before the live CURRENT STATEMENT at :905 with no matching END and seeded a stale figure on it: rc=0, 'OK: every surface agrees with the ledger rows.' One line, no error, no warning, and the run still reports a clean sweep. Section 4 of the spec tests only a BALANCED pair (it wraps a stale token in BEGIN...END and asserts exempt, then asserts the same token fires outside). I also verified the SHIPPED ledger is safe today: 5 BEGIN (854, 887, 1191, 1307, 1328) and 5 END (872, 903, 1202, 1324, 1337), correctly ordered and nested, so nothing live is currently hidden. Separately I neutralised all three markers and re-ran: the 13 things the exemptions currently hide are all genuinely historical (the 11/6/0/1, 10/6/1/1, 10/7/0/1, 9/8/0/1, 11/6/1/0 movement figures; v4.1.0's 13/3/0/0/16 at :945/:1194/:1200; and the DP5/DP3/DP4 old-verdict citations at :856/:1308/:1331, each inside an explicitly-labelled superseded block). No claim is smuggled under a sentinel.
findings.description: The operator's question (b) answered: yes, there is a way to silence the guard that the spec does not cover -- an unbalanced sentinel. The test file itself names this risk in its own words ('a history-block escape hatch that nothing tests is a way to silence the guard by wrapping the whole file') and then tests the balanced case, which is not the cheapest way to wrap the file; deleting one END is. I am NOT calling the test's text false: the assertion it claims to make does exist and does pass, and the shipped tree is balanced, so no current claim is affected -- hence INFO. v5.0.1 fix is small and self-checking: have strip_exempt count BEGIN/END and make an unbalanced file an exit-2 infra error rather than a silent exemption, and add the negative control (unmatched BEGIN + stale token must FAIL, not pass). That also guards the accidental case, which is the likely one: deleting an END while editing silently drops coverage over a span with no signal at all.

findings.evidence: STOP-RULE SIDE: added precision on a true claim -> NOT blocking, v5.0.1 follow-up. MEASURED, two mutations. (1) Delete EVERY '| PROVEN-WITH-CAVEAT | n |' table row from the ledger: got is empty, '[ -n "$got" ] || continue' fires, rc=0, 'OK: every surface agrees' -- the status silently stops being checked. (2) Delete only the CURRENT section's row (:840), leaving earlier releases' tables: 'grep ... | tail -1' then picks the v4.1.0 table's row at :623 and the tool reports 'TABLE: tally table says PROVEN-WITH-CAVEAT=3, ledger rows give 9' -- it fails, correctly, but names a figure belonging to a different release, which would send a reader to the wrong table. Controls confirm the check is otherwise sound: a present-but-wrong row fires accurately (M6b: says 7, gives 9), and moving a real row verdict (DP9 -> PROVEN) fires comprehensively on 2 TABLE + 2 TOKEN disagreements.
findings.description: check_table treats a missing row as 'nothing to compare' rather than as a defect, so deleting a row is an undetected way to stop the table being checked -- the same 'a check that stops checking' family the file's own --surface handling explicitly refuses ('a surface that silently vanished is how a check stops checking'). The inconsistency is worth naming: the script fails loudly on a vanished SURFACE and silently on a vanished table ROW. v5.0.1: make an absent status row a FAILURE (the current section must publish all four), and scope check_table to the current section the way check_tokens/check_citations already are via strip_exempt's second argument, so 'tail -1' cannot reach a prior release's table.

findings.evidence: STOP-RULE SIDE: added precision on a true claim -> NOT blocking, v5.0.1 follow-up. MEASURED: I appended each of five citation variants naming DP4 (ledger row: PROVEN-WITH-CAVEAT) as PROVEN to a ledger copy and ran the shipped checker. Only 'row `DP4`, PROVEN' fired (rc=1, 1 CITATION). All four of these passed silently at rc=0: 'DP4 is PROVEN' (no backticks), '`DP4` -- PROVEN' (dash separator), '`DP4` moved to PROVEN' (copula outside the is/was/now/remains set), '`DP4` (PROVEN)' (parenthesised).
findings.description: The citation check recognises the house style and essentially nothing else. That is a deliberate, documented and well-argued choice -- the header records that the loose 'id and verdict anywhere on the same line' form raised nine hits and every one was legitimate history, and 'a check that fires on correct prose trains its reader to ignore it' is correct. So this is not a defect and not a false claim; it is a bound on the guarantee that a reader of a green run should know. Recorded because the bound is invisible from the output: a clean run prints 'OK: every surface agrees with the ledger rows', which reads stronger than 'no tightly-formatted citation disagrees'. v5.0.1, if wanted: widen the copula set to include 'moved to' / 'remains at', accept an em-dash or parenthesis as the separator, and keep everything else as-is -- each of those is still adjacent, so none reintroduces the nine historical false positives.

findings.evidence: STOP-RULE SIDE: added precision on a true claim -> NOT blocking, v5.0.1 follow-up. The comment justifying why non-ledger surfaces are scanned whole reads: 'every other surface is scanned whole, because a surface that carries no frozen prior-release ledger has no legitimate reason to state a different tally anywhere in it.' CHANGELOG.md is by construction a document of frozen prior-release figures, and it already carries one: CHANGELOG.md:3840-3841 publishes v4.0.0's tally as 'PROVEN 51 / PROVEN-WITH-CAVEAT 47 / REMOVED 23 / NOT-PROVEN 0'. It does not fire today only because that is prose with words interleaved, not a bare five-group numeric token -- I confirmed by grep that CHANGELOG.md and README.md contain ZERO five-group tokens, so check_tokens currently has nothing at all to compare on either surface.
findings.description: The premise behind the scoping decision does not hold for a changelog, which is the one document type whose whole purpose is to preserve superseded figures. Nothing is wrong today, and the shipped tree is consistent -- hence INFO. The trap is deferred rather than absent: the moment a release's CHANGELOG entry states its tally in the five-group form the tool recognises, the NEXT release makes it a false positive that has to be wrapped in TALLY-HISTORY, and the person hitting it will be reading a comment that says this cannot happen. Worth one sentence in v5.0.1 either way: either correct the rationale, or give CHANGELOG.md the same current-section scoping the ledger gets, keyed on its '## [x.y.z]' headings. Related observation, recorded because a green run should not be over-read: the guard covers the FIGURE and VERDICT half of the recurring finding class, and R6-F1 above is in the PROPOSITION half, which the guard does not and by design cannot cover. A green release-claims-check does not mean the release text is consistent; it means no tally token or tight citation disagrees.
